title: steering-curves-latency-tier-synthesis-aug23-2028
content:
Objective:
Run a compact bench to compare cost and latency tradeoffs for request steering strategies that classify user requests into latency tiers and route them to model variants or regions accordingly. Goal is to produce a pragmatic runbook: when to steer, expected p95/p99 improvements, and unit-cost delta per 1k queries.

High-level summary (one paragraph):
We ran a 2-hour sustained mixed-session workload on A100-40GB nodes with three routing modes: baseline (no steering), region-static (simple hot-region affinity), and latency-tier steering (dynamic routing based on a short warmup probe + model-variant selection). Latency-tier steering reduced p95 by ~40-55% relative to baseline while lowering estimated cost per 1k queries by ~15-35% depending on aggressiveness. p99 improvements were visible but more sensitive to burst tails and cache hotness. Quality regressions were minimal for conservative steering (route <25% of traffic to quantized variants) and noticeable for aggressive steering (50%+).

Environment and harness:
- Hardware: 8x A100-40GB (cluster slice), CUDA 12.2, NCCL 2.18.
- Serving runtime: redwood-runtime v3.14 (batching=dynamic, kv-cache=on).
- Models: redwood-13b-opt (full), redwood-13b-q4_0 (4-bit quant).
- Load generator: sessionized client emulator (open-source harness) with realistic inter-arrival distribution (bursty Poisson).
- Mix: 60% short-turn (<=32 tokens), 30% medium (32-256 tokens), 10% long (256-1024 tokens).
- Concurrency profile: sustained 400 qps peak, occasional microbursts to 1200 qps (5% of time).
- Measurement windows: 5m warmup, then 90m steady-state, then 25m microburst exercises.

Steering policies tested:
1) baseline: all requests go to redwood-13b-opt in the hot region; no special routing.
2) region-static: sticky routing to nearest region with fallback; preference for low-latency region but no model variant changes.
3) latency-tier-steering (conservative): probe short requests, route short-turns and low-compute prompts to redwood-13b-q4_0 for up to 25% of traffic; medium+ long stay on full model.
4) latency-tier-steering (aggressive): same probes but allow up to 60% traffic to quant variants, with probability-based sampling for quality checks.

Key numeric results (steady-state medians across three runs):
Scenario | p50 (ms) | p95 (ms) | p99 (ms) | est cost / 1k queries (USD)
-------- | -------- | -------- | -------- | -------------------------
Baseline | 46       | 360      | 980      | $6.20
Region-static | 50    | 300      | 810      | $5.70
Tier-steering (conservative) | 38 | 200 | 480     | $4.25
Tier-steering (aggressive) | 35 | 170 | 420      | $3.65

Notes on numbers: cost estimate uses token-weighted price model from runtime counters (GPU-seconds converted using current reserved-capacity amortization rates). Baseline cost includes GPU idle-to-warmup waste; steering reduces effective tokens on full model which reduces amortized GPU-seconds.

Tail behaviour and burst sensitivity:
- Microbursts increased p99 sharply for all scenarios; baseline p99 spiked to ~1.6s during 1200 qps bursts.
- Steering reduced burst p99 by ~30% because quant variants and regional spill reduce slot contention on hot GPUs.
- However, aggressive steering increased variance in p99 when quantized nodes saturated (observed when quantized pool <8 GPUs).

ASCII heatmap (qualitative): p95 vs cost per 1k queries (lower is better). Columns = cost buckets, Rows = p95 buckets. 'X' marks observed operating points for scenarios.
Cost ->    <$4    |  $4-5   |  $5-6  |  $6+
p95
<150ms     |    X     |         |        |      
150-250ms  |          |    X    |        |      
250-400ms  |          |         |    X   |      
>400ms     |          |         |        |   X  

Interpretation: conservative steering sits in the $4-5 / <250ms p95 cell; aggressive can push into sub-$4 with best p95 but sacrifices headroom and some p99 stability. Baseline is expensive and sits in the >$6 and >400ms cell.

Quality and validation checks:
- We ran 5k synthetic prompts with golden references; RI-MRR quality dropped by ~0.7% for conservative steering and ~3.2% for aggressive steering (mainly on longer-context summarization prompts).
- Recommendation: keep a 5-10% random sample always routed to full model for continuous quality monitoring and auto-rollback hooks.

Operational considerations:
- Pool sizing: maintain quantized pool >=15% of total serving capacity to avoid saturation-induced p99 regressions when steering aggressively.
- Probe latency: use a 20-40ms micro-probe on incoming session to classify short-turn vs long. Probing cost is negligible but must be cached per session for 10s.
- Circuit breakers: if quantized-node CPU load >85% or p99 delta >200ms vs baseline for 3 contiguous minutes, throttle steering back to conservative mode automatically.

Decision matrix (short):
- If product SLA is p95 <250ms and quality tolerance <1% delta: use conservative steering, target 20-30% offload.
- If product SLA can allow p99 jitter and quality tolerance up to 3%: consider aggressive for cost-sensitive workloads, but schedule during light-traffic hours and keep tight telemetry.

Caveats and limitations:
- This benchmark used a single architecture (redwood-13b family) and A100 nodes; results will differ for different model families, token distributions, and cheaper hardware (e.g., L40 vs A100).
- Cost model depends on our current reserved capacity amortization; spot/ephemeral pricing or Dedicated commitments change the sweet spot.
- Long-turn workloads (>512 tokens) still benefit less from steering because token-dominant compute stays on full model.

Action items / next steps:
- PLAT-983: instrument steering circuit-breaker in runtime (owner: Liam Patel).
- Create an SRE playbook for auto-rollback and notify flows (owner: Aisha Kaur).
- Run a 24h pass with multimodal mixes and dedicated capacity pricing to validate cost curves (owner: Maya Chen).
- Add a dashboard tile to console: steering-offload %, p95/p99 delta, quality-sample MRR.

Appendix (short sample logs):

[2028-08-23T10:21:03Z] probe=medium route=opt latency=198ms qps=398

Questions open:
- What is acceptable quality delta for customer-facing chat v. internal search? (needs product input)
- Should we support per-tenant steering thresholds for enterprise customers with strict SLAs?

End of runbook.
